bullets.title: GOOGL: Massive $80B equity raise to fund AI infrastructure; Berkshire Hathaway invests $10B
bullets.body: Alphabet announced a $30B underwritten offering ($15B mandatory convertible preferred + $15B common stock, each with 15% greenshoe) plus a $40B at-the-market program starting Q3'26 and a $10B Berkshire Hathaway private placement ($5B Class A at $351.81, $5B Class C at $348.20). Proceeds earmarked for AI infrastructure and global compute capex; Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley are bookrunners with pricing June 2 post-close. Transaction is covered (aggregate demand exceeds offering amount).

bullets.title: HPE: Blowout Q2, raises FY26 guide 40%, Elliott names board member — stock +30%
bullets.body: HPE Q2 revenue $10.68B beat consensus $9.78B; EPS $0.79 vs $0.53 est; networking revenue +148% YoY to $2.7B. FY26 EPS guidance raised to $3.35–3.45 from $2.30–2.50 and revenue growth guide lifted to +29–33% from +17–22%; free cash flow guidance raised to $3.5B+ from $2.0B+. Elliott Management increased its stake 47% to 27.4M shares and named partner Chris Hsu to the board immediately; HPE hit F28 targets two years early and introduced FY27 framework of 8–12% revenue growth and $4.5B FCF.

bullets.title: CRDO: Post-earnings -12% as guidance missed elevated buyside bar despite beat
bullets.body: CRDO Q4 revenue $437M vs $431.8M guide (beat), EPS $1.16 vs $1.02 est; FY26 revenue tripled YoY to $1.3B and non-GAAP net income up 5x. Shares fell ~12% as buyside had expected another FY guide raise (April guide already up 25%) and commentary signaled apprehension on frontier model operator deployment pace; at $200, stock trades at 22.2x JPM FY28 EPS of ~$9.

bullets.title: NVDA: RTX Spark (AI PC chip) enters production; Vera Rubin at full production — stock +6%
bullets.body: NVIDIA launched RTX Spark, an ARM-based PC chip (N1X Grace CPU + Blackwell GPU) co-developed with Microsoft and Dell, targeting fall 2026 in 30+ laptops and 10 desktops; Jensen Huang called it a 'new beginning' on par with the smartphone revolution. Separately, the Vera Rubin multi-rack pod-scale platform entered full production for agentic AI factories. Analysts at Citi ($300 PT), KeyBanc ($310 PT), and Stifel ($282 PT) remain bullish; JPM noted the announcements pressure CPU rivals INTC and AMD with limited near-term volume risk. NVDA also disclosed projected revenues of ~$400B this year and ~$600B next, with networking expected to generate 20x the annual revenue of its PC chip segment.

bullets.title: ARM: Barclays raises PT to $360 from $250; stock surges from $134 to $413 in 2.5 months
bullets.body: Barclays lifted its ARM price target to $360 (from $250) citing NVIDIA RTX Spark's Grace CPU adoption and Morgan Stanley sees ARM benefiting from the push into agentic edge AI. ARM stock rose from $134 to $413 in approximately 2.5 months (+208%); one trader noted it was the highest-returning position in their portfolio. The shift from centralized cloud AI to distributed edge agents increases ARM architecture royalty potential.

bullets.title: Software sector: Best 2-day outperformance vs SPX in 25+ years; IGV call volume hits record
bullets.body: GS TMT desk notes software outperformed the S&P 500 by >1,000bps over two sessions, the largest stretch in ~25 years; IGV total call volume hit record 280k contracts Friday and 225k Monday. JPM attributed the move largely to short covering and positioning unwinds with investors reluctant to assign fundamental theses. SNOW earnings were cited as the spark; DDOG, SNOW, MDB posted blow-out prints while enterprise SaaS (NOW, CRM, ADBE) rallied on mixed earnings. Software stocks are now up 14%+ in 3 days (best since October 2001) but Jefferies notes MSFT, NET, PLTR are still -24% from all-time highs.

bullets.title: CRM: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform on Contentful acquisition; $220 PT
bullets.body: Salesforce is acquiring Contentful (headless CMS, $200M+ ARR, 4,800+ brands, 30% of Fortune 500 as customers) in a deal expected to close FQ3'27. Wolfe Research upgrades CRM to Outperform with a $220 PT (15.1% upside from $191), citing strategic fit with Headless 360 strategy and potential 0.5pt FY28 Commerce Cloud growth uplift.

bullets.title: AVGO: UBS raises PT to $490; Anthropic XPU arrangement significantly improves margins; AVGO earnings webcast 6/4
bullets.body: UBS raised AVGO PT to $490, noting that the Anthropic order was converted from a standard arrangement to an XPU/ASIC format at 3.5GW scale — reducing CY26 revenue contribution from $21B to $8B but significantly improving margins; Meta XPU expected to scale to $13B by FY2028 and OpenAI revenues modeled at ~$16B by FY2028. Wolfe Research is hosting a 15-minute post-earnings webcast with AVGO management on Thursday June 4 at 8:30am ET. Separately, JPM flagged a negative supply chain check suggesting MediaTek's Humufish TPU may be displacing AVGO at Google TPUv9.

bullets.title: TSM: All-time high (+7.2%); TSMC Arizona Phase 1 profitability surges; N3 remains AI bottleneck
bullets.body: TSM hit an all-time high up 7.2% on NVIDIA PC chip catalyst momentum. TSMC posted +41% YoY growth in 1Q26 with record gross and operating margins; Arizona Phase 1 net profit in 1Q26 alone exceeded all of CY25; board approved record single-tranche Arizona authorization on May 13. The N3 node remains the primary supply bottleneck of the AI cycle; foundry industry hit record $48.8B in 1Q26 (+32% YoY) with TSMC's share widening to 95%+.

bullets.title: MRVL: Teralynx T100 102.4 Tbps switch silicon launched; S&P 500 addition candidate June 5
bullets.body: Marvell introduced Teralynx T100, the industry's first 102.4 Tbps switch silicon purpose-built for AI workloads. Separately, quant models rank MRVL as the #1 S&P 500 addition candidate for announcement post-market June 5 at 5:15pm ET. VRT also appears high on the candidate list.

bullets.title: MU: Market cap tops $1T (+145% from prior report); options premium exceeds SPY+QQQ combined
bullets.body: Micron's market cap surpassed $1 trillion, representing a 10x+ increase over the past year; one analyst notes MU is up 145% since their prior report generating $325k for a single trader. Options premiums at open surpassed SPY and QQQ combined ($1.4B), a pattern last seen in NVDA in July 2024. Anthropic's confidential S-1 filing is viewed as a bullish read-through for AI infrastructure chip suppliers including MU, NVDA, SNDK, and LITE.

bullets.title: NBIS: Up 18%+ today (+212% YTD); 'king of neoclouds' nearing $60B market cap
bullets.body: Nebius (NBIS) extended gains +18.2% on the day, now +212% YTD with market cap at ~$60B; the stock is up 14% specifically from Jensen Huang's Computex presentations. Analysts view NBIS as the best-positioned neocloud player while CRWV is flagged for high debt interest and IREN for structural dilution via infinite ATMs. CRWV also completed the industry-first bring-up of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72. IREN separately closed a $3.65B investment-grade GPU financing facility for Microsoft AI Cloud delivery.

bullets.title: AAOI: +20% today; trader cites 80% options gain; bullish on photonics inflection H1 2027
bullets.body: AAOI surged 20.1% on the day; one trader reported 80% gains on Friday call options and described AAOI as their favorite US optical long, citing a photonics supercycle inflection expected to accelerate into H2 2027. Historical context: LITE is up 1,000%+ and COHR +300% after each received $2B NVIDIA investments in March. Citron's prior AAOI short during the last supercycle was noted as a losing trade, arguing against shorting here.

bullets.title: TTD: Nate Olmstead appointed CFO effective July 9, 2026
bullets.body: The Trade Desk appointed Nate Olmstead as permanent CFO effective July 9, replacing interim CFO Tahnil Davis (who returns to Chief Accounting Officer), describing the hire as supporting 'sustained accelerated growth and scale.'

bullets.title: APP: Citi adds 90-day upside catalyst watch on eCommerce platform moving to general availability
bullets.body: Citi adds AppLovin to its upside catalyst watch list with a 90-day horizon. The eCommerce platform is transitioning from a pilot/referral model to general availability by June 30, 2026, which should open the platform significantly and accelerate store growth; AppLovin is increasing Axon marketing in preparation.

bullets.title: DELL: Upgraded to equal-weight at Morgan Stanley (PT $448 from $170) on NVDA PC chip catalyst
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded Dell from underweight to equal-weight and raised its price target to $448 from $170, citing better memory management and pricing power driven by NVIDIA's RTX Spark PC chip partnership. Dell is included in the RTX Spark laptop/desktop launch (10+ desktop form factors), and Dell server revenue grew 100% YoY though HPE showed better-than-feared AI adoption.

bullets.title: CEG: -7.7% after pricing 11M share offering at $281; sector down 3%+ on renewable weakness
bullets.body: Constellation Energy priced an 11M share follow-on at $281/share and plans a 2M share buyback; the stock fell 7.7%. The broader S&P 500 Utilities Index fell 3% and Electric Utilities Index -3.4%, with ENPH -6.8% and BE -4.1% on sector weakness. Data center moratoriums are a growing regulatory theme with Texas counties and Pennsylvania legislation (H.B. 1834) emerging as headwinds for power-intensive infrastructure.

bullets.title: WBD: Upgraded to overweight from underweight at Huber Research
bullets.body: Warner Bros. Discovery was upgraded to overweight from underweight by analyst Douglas Arthur at Huber Research Partners; the stock closed at $27.27.

bullets.title: INTC: Pressured by NVDA PC chip launch; Intel Foundry EMIB+18A positioned as multi-billion franchise through 2028
bullets.body: Intel shares fell 6.7% at market open as NVIDIA's RTX Spark launch (Arm-based, targeting premium laptop/desktop) overshadows Intel's planned year-end AI data center inference chip with cheaper memory/cooling. On the foundry side, Intel's EMIB plus 18A-P/T roadmap is positioned as a multi-billion-dollar external franchise through 2028 with new competitive entrants including Rapidus (2nm) and Tata ramping.

bullets.title: GS TMT desk: Sector rotation context — Memory/NVDA/TSM resilient; Mag 7 underperforming
bullets.body: GS TMT desk notes NDX equal-weight outperformed NDX by ~86bps (largest 1-day spread since late March); NVDA +6%, AVGO and MSFT both +8% over two days vs META -5.5% and AMZN -4.5%. HPE +30% (now ~100% in 3 weeks); CRDO -12%. Gig economy outperformed: UBER +5%, DASH +3.5%, CART +6%. ISM at 54.0 (4-year high) supported risk appetite; GS TMT Momentum pair pulled back ~600bps.
